turns.user: My uncle has occupied our ancestral land near Nashik worth about 3 crores and has forged my late father's signature on a sale deed. What should I do?
turns.reply:
This situation is extremely serious. Because this involves high-value ancestral land and a claim that a legal document (a sale deed) was forged, you need to consult a lawyer as a matter of urgency. A property title dispute of this size requires a professional who can examine the documents and represent you in court to protect your ownership rights.

### Understanding where you stand
Forgery is a criminal offence under the *Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023* [[BNS2023:s336]]. If a document like a sale deed (which is considered a "valuable security") has been forged, it carries severe penalties, including imprisonment [[BNS2023:s338]]. 

Legally, you have the right to challenge the validity of such a document. The *Limitation Act, 1963* provides a period of three years to file a suit to declare an instrument as a forgery, starting from the time you first became aware of the forgery [[LIM1963:art56]]. 

### Recommended next steps
1.  **Do not wait:** Please seek a lawyer in Nashik immediately. A lawyer will help you file the appropriate civil suit to challenge the sale deed and, if necessary, initiate criminal proceedings for the forgery.
2.  **Gather documents:** Collect any proof of your father's ownership, such as the original land records, tax receipts, and the death certificate. If you have any copy or proof of the alleged sale deed, take that to your lawyer as well.
3.  **Check land records:** Visit the local land record office (the Talathi office or Sub-Registrar's office in Nashik) to get the most recent '7/12 extract' (land record). This will show whose name is currently recorded as the owner.
4.  **Legal Aid:** If you need assistance finding a lawyer, you can reach out to the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) helpline at **15100**. They can guide you toward free or affordable legal aid services in your area [[NOTE:NALSA]].

I cannot represent you in court, and I cannot verify the specific facts of your property title, but a local lawyer will be able to guide you on the best way to regain control of the land and hold your uncle accountable.

To help me give you more specific information for your lawyer:
*   Do you have a copy of the alleged sale deed, or do you know when it was allegedly registered?
*   Is your name or your father's name currently recorded as the owner in the government land records (the 7/12 extract)?
